Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Law 13/2021 of 28 April, which strengthened beneficial-ownership identification and reporting; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales); Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act; applicable EU AML legislation, including Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Capital Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registered-office and correspondence purposes if it provides a genuine address, mail handling, corporate records access, and legally effective notices. It is not sufficient as the sole operational substance for high-precision injection molding, assembly, warehousing, inventory, product-safety compliance, or manufacturing activity. The company should maintain appropriate premises, equipment, supply-chain records, accounting records, and personnel or outsourced operational capacity proportionate to its activities.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation, Madrid) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (definitive inscription); notarization before a Spanish Notario.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 9 (registered office), 20-24 (formation and deed of incorporation), 25-26 (inscription in the Mercantile Registry), 58-62 (share capital and certified payment), 175-197 (general meeting), 209-232 (administrators); Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre (SL de Formación Sucesiva regime).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) granted before a notary and inscribed in the Registro Mercantil Provincial; accompanying filings include Modelo 600 (AJD stamp-duty self-assessment) and Modelo 036 (AEAT census declaration for definitive NIF). Costs consist of regulated notarial and registry tariffs plus AJD (approx. EUR 30 for EUR 3,000 capital); there is no centralized state filing fee.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 33 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; payment evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) or by a valuation expert report for in-kind contributions. Alternative: SL de Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) allows EUR 1 paid-up capital subject to statutory restrictions (mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until capital and reserves reach EUR 3,000; prohibition of interim dividends; reduced member ceiling of 5). Non-resident founders may hold 100% of quotas and require a Spanish NIE.

Funding & unlock path: Fire-safety certification of the industrial premises under Real Decreto 2267/2004 (Reglamento de seguridad contra incendios en los establecimientos industriales) with a technical project and municipal fire-department inspection; building structural-load certificate for injection-molding machines; occupational risk-prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 and workplace-conditions compliance under Real Decreto 486/1997 (workplaces), Real Decreto 1215/1997 (work equipment), Real Decreto 773/1997 (personal protective equipment), and Real Decreto 842/2002 (REBT electrical installations); appointment of a prevention service and registration of the risk-prevention plan, employee training records, and medical-surveillance protocols.

Paid-in capital rule: Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; payment evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) or by a valuation expert report for in-kind contributions. Alternative: SL de Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) allows EUR 1 paid-up capital subject to statutory restrictions (mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until capital and reserves reach EUR 3,000; prohibition of interim dividends; reduced member ceiling of 5). Non-resident founders may hold 100% of quotas and require a Spanish NIE.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED, unanimously, by the founding members of [●], S.L., convened as the inaugural general meeting: First, to approve the draft articles of association and subscribe in full the initial share capital of EUR 3,000.00, fully paid in cash, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate under Article 62 of the Capital Companies Act, with shareholdings as set forth in the deed. Second, to adopt the registered office at [●], province of [●], and to ratify a corporate object comprising manufacture of toys and hobby goods under ISIC 3240. Third, to appoint [●] as Sole Administrator and [●] as Secretary, both accepting office, and to authorize the Sole Administrator to complete all notarial, registry, tax, and banking formalities.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Consejería de Industria / Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas of the relevant Autonomous Community (regional industrial authority) in coordination with the Ayuntamiento (municipal government) for activity and opening licensing; the central industrial database is the Registro Integrado Industrial (RII). Toy manufacture itself is not subject to prior sectoral authorization in Spain — market access requires CE marking under Real Decreto 1205/2011 — but physical operation of an industrial plant requires municipal activity licensing and the pre-commencement communication to the industrial registry.

Category: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (or Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad for low-risk activities under municipal ordinances implementing Directive 2006/123/CE and Ley 39/2015); plus Comunicación de Puesta en Marcha del Establecimiento Industrial (Ley 21/1992, de Industria, art. 14, as implemented by regional industry regulations); toy CE conformity under Real Decreto 1205/2011, de 26 de agosto (transposing Directive 2009/48/CE).

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); business census registry: Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores; commercial incorporation registry: Registro Mercantil Central.

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) owned by non-residents: (1) each non-resident founder obtains an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) from the Spanish Consulate or local immigration office; (2) reserve the company name at the Registro Mercantil Central (certificación de denominación social); (3) file modelo 036 with AEAT to obtain a provisional NIF prior to notarisation; (4) execute the public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) before a Spanish notary, deposit it at the Registro Mercantil, and file modelo 600 (TIE/JP) for capital transfer tax formalities; (5) within 30 days of deed registration, submit modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (for an SL: letter 'B' + 7 digits + control character); (6) register in the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores and, if annual turnover exceeds EUR 1 million or intra-EU acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000, obtain a NIF-IVA (VAT identification number); (7) secure an electronic certificate (FNMT digital certificate) for mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT portal; (8) foreign entities without a permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain, registered via modelo 036.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation (Impuesto sobre Sociedades; general CIT rate 25%; reduced 15% for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base). Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for tax-resident SLs; foreign partners are taxed under Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) only on Spanish-source income. Tax-Exempt Zone: Canary Islands ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) offers 4% CIT and reduced VAT (IGIC) for approved manufacturing/trading entities established in the Canary Islands. No pass-through transparency for Spanish SLs. — For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) owned by non-residents: (1) each non-resident founder obtains an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) from the Spanish Consulate or local immigration office; (2) reserve the company name at the Registro Mercantil Central (certificación de denominación social); (3) file modelo 036 with AEAT to obtain a provisional NIF prior to notarisation; (4) execute the public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) before a Spanish notary, deposit it at the Registro Mercantil, and file modelo 600 (TIE/JP) for capital transfer tax formalities; (5) within 30 days of deed registration, submit modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (for an SL: letter 'B' + 7 digits + control character); (6) register in the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores and, if annual turnover exceeds EUR 1 million or intra-EU acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000, obtain a NIF-IVA (VAT identification number); (7) secure an electronic certificate (FNMT digital certificate) for mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT portal; (8) foreign entities without a permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain, registered via modelo 036.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation (Impuesto sobre Sociedades; general CIT rate 25%; reduced 15% for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base). Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for tax-resident SLs; foreign partners are taxed under Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) only on Spanish-source income. Tax-Exempt Zone: Canary Islands ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) offers 4% CIT and reduced VAT (IGIC) for approved manufacturing/trading entities established in the Canary Islands. No pass-through transparency for Spanish SLs.

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box; elections embedded in Spanish law: (1) tax consolidation regime for groups with 75%+ ownership (Art. 64-79 LIS); (2) merger/reorganisation neutrality regime deferring built-in gains (Art. 76-89 LIS); (3) 15% reduced CIT for new SLs (Art. 29.3 LIS) tapering to 25% thereafter; (4) ETVE/participation-exemption election for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS); (5) cash-basis VAT (criterio de caja) for SMEs with turnover up to EUR 2 million, deferred VAT payment until customer payment; (6) monthly VAT refund regime for regular exporters (election via modelo 036 enabling refunds in each monthly 303 return); (7) EU SME VAT exemption election (from 1 Jan 2025) for businesses with turnover up to EUR 85,000 domestic / EUR 100,000 intra-EU; (8) cross-border loss relief and foreign tax credit elections under the LIS anti-double-taxation framework (Art. 31-32 LIS).

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general domestic monetary threshold: any person commencing taxable economic activity in Spanish territory must register in the Censo de Empresarios (modelo 036/037) before the first transaction, regardless of turnover. Optional SME exemption effective 1 Jan 2025: businesses with annual turnover in Spain below EUR 85,000 and intra-EU cross-border supplies below EUR 100,000 may elect full VAT exemption; otherwise registration is mandatory and VAT applies from the first sale.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of ISIC 3240 mecha model kits to non-EU buyers are exempt with refund (0% IVA) under Art. 21 LIVA provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch (AEAT may extend to 180 days on justified request) and the exporter retains accepted documentary proof of exit. Intra-EU zero-rated supplies under Art. 25 LIVA require the customer's valid EU VAT number recorded in the VIES database, dispatch of goods to another Member State, and filing of the recapitulative EC Sales List (modelo 349) plus Intrastat if the annual threshold is exceeded. Export-related services (international transport, loading, customs agency, design and offshore support services supplied to non-EU customers) are also zero-rated. The exporter must demonstrate that it holds the goods, is the declarant, and that the export invoice is issued in the name of the exporter; e-commerce export consignments may be zero-rated when dispatched with the parcel operator and covered by the exporter's DUA. Refunds of input VAT on export costs are claimed through the periodic modelo 303 return, or monthly under the devolución mensual election for regular exporters; non-established businesses use modelo 361 (Refund Directive) via the AEAT portal.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) lodged electronically and accepted by the Customs Office of departure, with the Export Accompanying Document (EAD) and indication of exit via the NCTS system
  • Proof of exit of the goods: Bill of Lading (maritime), Air Waybill (air), CMR road consignment note, or customs exit-stamped copy of the Single Administrative Document issued or validated by the Customs office of exit
  • Commercial invoice, packing list, P&L weight/unit price documentation, and bank payment certificate (inward remittance certificate/certificado de cobro) evidencing collection of export proceeds; for intra-EU supplies also the EC Sales List (modelo 349) and Intrastat declaration

Near-real-time fiscal clearance via SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory for taxpayers with turnover > EUR 6,010,121.41 or in consolidated VAT groups; invoice records must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 for certain records) of issue via web service/API. Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, applicable from 2025): all invoicing software must generate non-editable, hash-chained invoice records and display a QR Verifactu on each invoice, allowing AEAT real-time access to invoice integrity. Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) mandates structured B2B e-invoicing (Facturae 3.2 XML or equivalent UN/CEFACT CII/UBL) with the implementing royal decree expected to phase in application one year after publication for enterprises > EUR 8 million turnover and two years for SMEs; B2G invoicing through the FACe platform is already compulsory. Exports are cleared through the electronic customs declaration (e-DUA) in the AEAT customs system, not by fiscal stamping of invoices.

AEAT verifies export exemption substantiation under Art. 23-24, 26 and 30 LIVA. Missing, defective, or fraudulent export documentation re-characterises the sale as a domestic taxable transaction at 21% IVA, with late-payment interest from the original due date, surcharges of 20%-35% (período ejecutivo), and a penalty under Art. 170 and 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the tax evaded where culpability is established. Criminal fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal (1-6 years imprisonment) applies when the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period; the four-year limitation period for the right to assess tax (10 years for fraudulently concealed gains) enables retrospective clawbacks. Although Spain imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, AEAT treats uncollected export receivables beyond 180 days from the DUA as a red flag requiring proof of collection; overdue balances may be reclassified as taxable income or deemed loans attracting imputation, and transactions with non-residents above EUR 50,000 must be reported to Banco de España in the Balance of Payments statistical declaration. The taxpayer bears the burden of proving the physical exit of goods and receipt of payment within the 90/180-day window.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain operates a fully convertible Euro regime. Capital account transactions are liberalized for EU counterparties with no prior approval required. Non-resident profit remittances are permitted after Spanish tax withholding and beneficial ownership verification. Hurdles include CRS/FATCA reporting obligations and potential CFC or anti-avoidance rules.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds to authorized dealers. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or applied to current account transactions. All exports require customs declaration, VAT-compliant invoicing, and annual corporate tax filing with no statutory conversion timeline.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

PayPal Fit: High

PayPal Business and similar EMI platforms are available to Spanish SL entities but subject to volume limits and cross-border restrictions. Legal constraints include mandatory NIF registration, full AML/KYC due diligence, and PSD2 compliance. Offshore digital EMIs face heightened scrutiny for transaction monitoring and tax reporting.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with IBAN, purpose codes such as 'Payment for goods' or 'Share capital injection', and matching invoices. Verification requires beneficial owner attestation, tax ID confirmation, and AML source-of-funds documentation.Outbound settlements via SWIFT MT103 or commercial Letters of Credit. Trade disbursements require supporting documentation including purchase orders, shipping documents, bills of lading, and tax-compliant invoices.Forward FX contractsNon-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs)Currency swapsFX options

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: PayPal Business and similar EMI platforms are available to Spanish SL entities but subject to volume limits and cross-border restrictions. Legal constraints include mandatory NIF registration, full AML/KYC due diligence, and PSD2 compliance. Offshore digital EMIs face heightened scrutiny for transaction monitoring and tax reporting.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory eligibility and anti-abuse conditions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, European Union relief, treaty reductions, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse rules, and procedural compliance. A qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are met.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200 is generally due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; for non-calendar tax years, the periods are calculated by reference to the fourth, tenth, and thirteenth months after the start of the tax year. Electronic filing deadlines are subject to AEAT calendar rules and extensions where the final day is not a permitted filing day.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 45,000,000 is the principal aggregate related-party transaction threshold commonly relevant to the exemption from full related-party documentation for taxpayers below the threshold, subject to transaction-specific exceptions and statutory documentation rules. A Local File may nevertheless be required for particular categories or transactions, including certain high-risk transactions. A Master File is generally relevant where the taxpayer belongs to a qualifying multinational or domestic group. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a separate regime branded as Economic Substance Regulations comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse principles require genuine commercial rationale, real functions, appropriate personnel, assets, decision-making, risk assumption, and documentary evidence. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the conflict-in-application rule, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, interest limitation rules, and principal-purpose analysis may deny benefits or recharacterize arrangements lacking substance. A Spanish SL manufacturing model-kit products should align its personnel, production assets, inventory, quality control, procurement, sales, and risk profile with its declared remuneration.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate income tax evasion and concealed income

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties may range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to assessment of tax, late-payment interest, and surcharges. Tax fraud may become a criminal offense where the amount of tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases carry higher penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil liability, subsidiary liability for tax debts where statutory conditions are met, disqualification consequences, and criminal liability. Courts may order restitution, asset seizure, and, in criminal cases, imprisonment. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed by judicial order where legally justified.
Value added tax fraud and carousel arrangements

Statutory sanction: VAT assessments, recovery of improperly claimed input VAT, interest, and administrative penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of the unpaid or improperly credited VAT. Serious or organized fraud may trigger criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and asset confiscation.

Director personal liability: Directors and persons who knowingly participate may incur civil and criminal liability. Company protection does not shield individuals who direct, authorize, or materially facilitate fraudulent VAT conduct.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income, deny deductions, impose transfer-pricing documentation penalties, assess late-payment interest, and apply penalties linked to the tax shortfall. Failure to provide required documentation can attract fixed penalties or percentage-based penalties subject to statutory limits.

Director personal liability: Directors may face derivative civil liability and, where deliberate falsification or tax fraud is established, criminal exposure. A formal group policy does not cure unsupported pricing or sham services.
Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse

Statutory sanction: Treaty benefits and domestic exemptions may be denied; withholding tax, interest, penalties, and anti-abuse adjustments may be assessed. Sham or fraudulent structures may generate criminal tax or commercial-law liability.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur tax, civil, and potentially criminal liability where they knowingly implement a sham structure. Courts may disregard artificial arrangements and order restitution or asset measures.
Unlawful profit extraction and disguised distributions

Statutory sanction: The amounts may be recharacterized as dividends, salary, or non-deductible expenses, generating corporate tax, personal income tax, withholding tax, social-security exposure, interest, and penalties. Unlawful distributions may also create corporate restitution claims.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable under Spanish company law for unlawful distributions, creditor damage, breach of fiduciary duties, and failure to preserve corporate assets.
AML, sanctions, and suspicious payment activity

Statutory sanction: AML breaches may result in significant administrative fines, public censure, temporary restrictions, and management disqualification. Sanctions violations may trigger separate administrative or criminal consequences, including asset blocking and confiscation.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face personal administrative or criminal liability where they knowingly participate in or negligently permit prohibited conduct.
Customs, import, product-safety, and intellectual-property violations

Statutory sanction: Consequences may include customs reassessment, seizure, destruction of goods, import restrictions, administrative fines, civil damages, and criminal prosecution for serious counterfeiting or fraud.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil compensation, injunctions, disqualification, and criminal liability where they knowingly authorize counterfeit imports, customs fraud, or unsafe product distribution.
Accounting falsification and corporate-record failures

Statutory sanction: Possible consequences include accounting sanctions, tax reassessment, commercial-registry consequences, creditor claims, director disqualification, and criminal penalties for materially false accounting or insolvency-related misconduct.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for creditor losses, wrongful trading, late insolvency filing, breach of accounting duties, and criminal falsification.
Unlawful permanent establishment or labor and social-security avoidance

Statutory sanction: Spain may assess corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding, social-security contributions, interest, and penalties. Labor violations may produce additional fines, back-pay obligations, and operational restrictions.

Director personal liability: Directors may face subsidiary liability for unpaid tax and social-security debts, labor claims, and criminal exposure where deliberate fraud, exploitation, or document falsification is established.
